FOREIGN COLORS | EPL PLAYBOOK
Research-informed application, not a proven outcome.

TITLE: A U.S. audience is not one giant away end.

IDEA: Learn how American followers first encountered the club. Co-create introductions with local supporter communities that connect the club’s history to their actual experiences.

BASIS: Transnational fandom and digital football culture provide context.

OBJECTIVE: Identify different routes into overseas attachment and barriers to participating from the U.S.

KPI: Reported discovery pathways, sense of welcome and repeat participation by newcomer cohort.

TEST: Pilot history-led, player-led and community-led introductions. Keep access and format comparable and interview participants about meaning.

CAUTION: Hong Kong findings cannot substitute for U.S. research. Avoid treating an American audience as culturally uniform.

SOURCES
R21: https://www.routledge.com/Digital-Football-Cultures-Fandom-Identities-and-Resistance/Crawford-Lawrence/p/book/9781351118903
R22: https://doi.org/10.1177/10126902221112779
See the website evidence library for links and limitations.
